reason: E2 and E3 directly state that fine-grained CoCrFeMnNi has higher surface strength, forms a less cracked oxide layer, and exhibits lower friction and wear rates compared to coarse-grained samples, supporting all key premises. E1 is only tangentially related, noting oxidation effects in HEA tribology but not grain size effects, and its mention of low friction in UHV without oxidation does not contradict the hypothesis.
premises: Finer grain size increases surface hardness in CoCrFeMnNi HEA
Finer grain size promotes a more stable, less cracked oxide tribolayer during sliding
A stable oxide tribolayer reduces friction coefficient and specific wear rate
Coarse grains soften under friction heat, leading to oxide layer fracture and plastic deformation
The oxide layer acts as a protective barrier reducing adhesive wear and delamination
